prompt:
You are an expert Roblox game developer, technical artist, and sound designer. Build a complete, playable, visually charming Roblox 3D platformer inspired by the original Spyro the Dragon trilogy (Insomniac, PS1). Single-player and drop-in co-op friendly. It must play and look great on ALL platforms: phone, tablet, PC, and console.

FIRST: produce a full Game Design Document (GDD) - game pillars and vision, target audience, core loop, movement and combat design, hub-and-level world structure, collectible/progression economy, enemy and boss design, art direction, audio direction, UI/UX and cross-platform input strategy, monetization philosophy (cosmetic-only, no pay-to-win), and success metrics. THEN produce a detailed technical implementation plan - architecture, module breakdown, instance hierarchy, data flow, and milestone order. THEN autonomously implement the entire plan end to end without waiting for further input: write all scripts, build/define all visual and audio systems, wire everything up, and deliver a working, good-looking, good-sounding game.

CORE MOVEMENT & COMBAT (the Spyro feel)
- Tight, responsive dragon movement: run, jump, double-jump, and a signature glide (hold to glide, descend slowly, with a dive/charge-into-glide flow). Air control that feels floaty-but-controlled.
- Charge: a horn-down dash that bowls over weak enemies, breaks charge-only gates/chests, and crosses gaps; can charge off ramps.
- Flame breath: ranged fire that torches flammable enemies and objects; some enemies must be charged not flamed, and vice versa (the classic metal-armor vs. flammable rule).
- Ground-pound/headbash as an unlockable; hover as an optional glide-extension unlock.
- Enemy variety: chargeable, flammable, shielded (must flank), and flying foes. Readable tells and knockback.

WORLD STRUCTURE
- Central hub worlds that portal into themed levels (grassy realm, lava caverns, ice cliffs, spooky night world, sky/cloud realm). Return-portal home stone in each level.
- Levels are open-ish 3D playgrounds with branching paths, hidden alcoves, and vertical secrets rewarding glide/charge mastery.
- A guide companion (dragonfly-style) that follows, gives hints, and acts as a hit buffer (lose it on hit, recover it from nearby critters) - classic Spyro health model.

COLLECTIBLES & PROGRESSION
- Gems (scattered, in chests, from enemies) as the primary currency - some hidden, some behind skill gates. Sparkle + chime on pickup, magnetize toward the player at close range.
- Trapped dragons / captured creatures to free as the milestone collectible that gates world progress.
- Eggs as rare hidden-challenge rewards. Per-level completion % and a total-completion tracker. Unlock cosmetics (scale colors, glide trails, flame colors) - no pay-to-win.

VISUAL QUALITY (bright, storybook, AAA-charming - not default Roblox)
- Warm, saturated, high-readability art direction: rounded stylized geometry, soft gradients, painterly skyboxes, gentle atmospheric fog for depth. Each realm gets a distinct palette and mood (sunny meadow, molten orange caverns, cool blue ice, purple haunted night).
- Lighting: Future lighting, Bloom + ColorCorrection + SunRays + subtle DepthOfField, per-realm color grade. Soft rim light on the dragon so it pops from backgrounds.
- Materials & maps: cohesive stylized PBR, clean silhouettes, strong focal lighting on portals, chests, and dragons-to-free. No flat untextured parts.
- VFX: flame breath as layered particles + light with heat shimmer; glide trail ribbons; gem sparkle and collect burst; charge dust and speed lines; portal swirl; enemy poof on defeat. Screen-space feedback on hit.
- Camera & feel: smooth follow-cam with auto-framing, gentle catch-up, glide pull-back for speed sense, subtle shake on charge impacts and landings, light hit-stop on flame kills, FOV kick on charge.
- Character: expressive dragon idle fidgets, flap/glide poses, charge lean, flame wind-up. Readable, cute, lively.
- Performance: pool particles, LOD distant geometry/VFX, streaming level loads, hold 60fps.

SOUND DESIGN (playful, orchestral, reactive)
- Dragon: flappy glide whoosh, charge gallop + wind rush, flame roar with crackle, jump/land grunts, footsteps by surface. 3D positional sound.
- World: gem pickup chime that rises in pitch on streaks, chest-smash, portal hum/swoosh, dragon-freed fanfare, egg-found jingle. Enemy poofs and stings.
- Music: melodic, whimsical orchestral per realm; adaptive layers that swell near combat or secrets; boss theme; victory/complete fanfare. Diegetic UI plips.
- Mixing: SoundGroups for SFX/Music/UI/Ambience with ducking under fanfares. Reverb zones (caverns vs. open sky). Per-realm 3D ambient beds (birds, wind, lava bubble, spooky wind). Master + per-bus volume in settings.

MOBILE & CROSS-PLATFORM (must play well on phone/tablet/console, not just PC)
- Detect input type and adapt: touch, mouse/keyboard, and gamepad all first-class. Never assume PC.
- Touch controls: on-screen thumbstick for movement; clear buttons for jump/glide (context-sensitive: hold jump to glide), charge, and flame; auto-face-nearest-enemy assist for flame/charge on touch.
- Auto-scaling UI: Scale-based UDim2 + anchor points so the HUD (gems, guide, health, level %) reflows for phone, tablet, and TV-safe zones. Large, thumb-reachable targets on mobile.
- Adaptive quality tiers: auto-detect device power and scale particles, dynamic lights, bloom/DOF, and draw distance down on mobile to hold 60fps (30fps floor). Manual quality toggle in settings.
- Camera: touch-drag look with sensible sensitivity and glide auto-align; full gamepad mapping with charge/flame aim assist.
- Test every system against touch and gamepad, not just PC input.

TECH
- Luau, server-authoritative where it matters (collectibles, progression, co-op enemy state); client-predicted movement for responsiveness. Anti-exploit checks on gem/egg awards; no client-trusted currency.
- Modular: MovementController, GlideSystem, CombatSystem (charge/flame), EnemyAI, CollectibleManager, World/PortalManager, ProgressionSaveManager, VFXManager, AudioManager, CameraController, InputManager (cross-platform), UI. Clean RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions. DataStore-backed saves with session locking.
- Custom animations for run/jump/glide/charge/flame; raycast ground/ledge detection; charge and glide physics tuned for game feel.

Deliver in this order: (1) the GDD, (2) the technical implementation plan, (3) all commented scripts, the folder/instance hierarchy, and VFX/lighting/audio setup, (4) setup steps. Implement the code in order: movement core → glide & charge feel → flame/combat & enemies → collectibles & progression → hub/portal world flow → cross-platform input & UI scaling. Work autonomously through every milestone until the game looks, sounds, and plays great on every device.

prompt:
Create the first playable version of a 3D multiplayer Roblox resource-gathering game.

For this step, build only the woodcutting system. Do not add trading, mining, shops, combat, quests, or other systems yet.

CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP

1. The player spawns in a small town center.
2. The player can walk from the town center into a nearby pine forest.
3. The player starts with a basic axe in their inventory.
4. The player equips the axe and walks up to a tree.
5. The player clicks or taps the tree to chop it.
6. Every successful chop gives the player exactly 1 Wood.
7. Wood is immediately added to the player's inventory.
8. A tree disappears after it has been chopped 10 times.
9. The tree respawns in the same location after a 30-second cooldown.
10. The player can continue chopping trees and collecting Wood.

WORLD

Create a simple but polished 3D environment with:

- A small medieval-style town center
- A dirt path leading into the forest
- A forest containing at least 20 pine trees
- Grass, rocks, bushes, and uneven terrain
- Clear separation between the town center and forest

The pine trees should look detailed and visually appealing. Each tree should have:

- A brown textured trunk
- Multiple layers of green pine branches
- Slight variation in height, width, and rotation
- A sturdy base that meets the ground naturally

WOODCUTTING

The axe should be a visible 3D tool held in the player's hand.

When the player chops:

- Play a short axe-swing animation
- Play a wood-chopping sound
- Show a small wood-chip particle effect
- Briefly shake the tree
- Prevent the player from chopping faster than once every 0.75 seconds

Each tree must track its own remaining health.

- Every tree starts with 10 health
- Each axe hit removes 1 health
- Each successful hit gives the player 1 Wood
- When health reaches 0, the tree disappears
- The tree cannot be chopped while it is gone
- The tree returns after 30 seconds with full health

MULTIPLAYER

Trees should be shared between all players in the server.

If multiple players chop the same tree, they should all be damaging the same tree. Each player receives 1 Wood only for the hits they personally make.

INVENTORY

Create a simple persistent inventory system.

For now, the inventory only needs to store:

- Wood

Display the player's Wood total on the screen using a small inventory counter.

Example:

Wood: 24

The player's Wood amount must save when they leave and load when they return using Roblox DataStoreService.

Make all inventory rewards and tree damage server-authoritative so players cannot easily exploit the system.

UI

Keep the UI simple and clean.

Add:

- A small Wood counter
- A basic inventory button
- An inventory panel that shows the Wood icon and quantity
- A short prompt near a tree that says "Equip Axe to Chop" when the axe is not equipped

Do not add unnecessary menus.

IMPORTANT

Build and test the game in small steps.

Prioritize:

- Reliable axe equipping
- Reliable tree hit detection
- Correct Wood rewards
- Tree disappearance and respawning
- Persistent inventory saving
- Multiplayer synchronization

Do not expand beyond this woodcutting loop.
